blocked.reason: "Entendido" violates the binding register rule that buttons and menus use the infinitive (es-419 convention; imperative is reserved for instructions/alarms). It is a past participle meaning "Understood", and its only consumer is the close button on sync toasts (src/components/SyncToast.tsx:61, aria-label) — including persistent sync-failure toasts — so it mislabels a dismiss action as an acknowledgment of the failure.
failedLenses: Register: usted, imperative for instructions, <=6th-grade reading level, phone-screen concision for labels/buttons

blocked.reason: Phone-row concision failure: the English placeholder is a terse 17-character hint ('For MEWP / height') inside a small numeric/text input, but the Spanish runs ~55 characters ('Para plataforma de trabajo aéreo (MEWP) / trabajo en altura'), roughly 3x the source. Input placeholders clip on phone screens, so the trailing '/ trabajo en altura' (and possibly '(MEWP)') will be truncated and unreadable, and the text vanishes as soon as the user types — a placeholder cannot carry a first-use acronym expansion.

blocked.reason: English source is "Pre-Task / Pre-Build Plan" but the Spanish "Plan previo a la tarea (PTP)" drops the entire "Pre-Build" half of the document name. Back-translation reads only "Pre-Task Plan", so Spanish-speaking crews doing pre-build/assembly work are no longer told this crew-signature legal document covers their activity — a dropped scope element on a legal form title. The glossary mandates "plan previo a la tarea (PTP)" for the Pre-Task Plan term but does not authorize deleting the Pre-Build alternative from this source string.
failedLenses: Safety accuracy: blind back-translation diff (ptp namespace) — dropped conditions, softened imperatives, flipped negations, weakened permit/legal meaning

blocked.reason: "Divida el trabajo en el orden real en que lo hará" is not idiomatic: 'dividir X en Y' requires Y to be the parts (steps), not the order. As written, a 6th-grade reader parses 'divide the job into the order', a grammatically odd object that forces a re-read — the 'into steps' object present in the concept is missing. The rest of the sentence and the second sentence are fine.
failedLenses: Register: usted, imperative for instructions, infinitive for buttons/menus, <=6th-grade, one action per sentence, phone-row concision
